source_text: Ἵνα δὲ μὴ δοκῶμεν ἑκόντες διὰ τὸ ἀπορεῖν ἀπαντήσεως ὑπερβαίνειν αὐτοῦ τὰ κεφάλαια, ἐκρίναμεν ἕκαστον κατὰ δύναμιν λῦσαι τῶν ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ προτιθεμένων. φροντίσαντες οὐ τοῦ ἐν τῇ φύσει τῶν πραγμάτων εἱρμοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθίας ἀλλὰ τῆς τάξεως τῶν ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ αὐτοῦ ἀναγεγραμμένων. φέρ᾿ οὖν ἴδωμεν, τί ποτε καὶ λέγει διαβάλλων τὸ οἷον σωματικῶς ἑωραμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος πνεῦμα ἅγιον εἴδει περιστερᾶς· ἔστι δ᾿ ὁ Ἰουδαῖος αὐτῷ ἔτι ταῦτα λέγων, πρὸς ὃν ὁμολογοῦμεν εἶναι κύριον ἡμῶν τὸν Ἰησοῦν· λουομένῳ, φησὶ, σοὶ παρὰ τῷ Ἰωάννῃ φάσμα ὄρνιθος ἐξ ἀέρος λέγεις ἐπιπτῆναι. εἶτα πυνθανόμενος ὁ παρ᾿ αὐτῷ Ἰουδαῖός φησι· τίς τοῦτο εἶδεν ἀξιόχρεως μάρτυς τὸ φάσμα, ἢ τίς ἤκουσεν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ φωνῆς εἰσποιούσης σε υἱὸν τῷ θεῷ; πλὴν ὅτι σὺ φῂς καί τινα ἕνα ἐπάγῃ τῶν μετὰ σοῦ κεκολασμένων.
pass_a_gloss: So that we may not seem to be dodging an answer out of being at a loss, we decided to solve each of the things proposed by him according to our ability, having taken care not of the natural connection and sequence of things, but of the order of the things written in his book. Come then, let us see what he says, slandering the Holy Spirit seen bodily by the Savior in the form of a dove; and the Jew says these things to him, to whom we confess to be our Lord Jesus; he says, 'You, being baptized by John, say that a phantom of a bird came down to you from the air.' Then the Jew with him, having inquired, says, 'Who is the worthy witness who saw the phantom, or who heard a voice from heaven calling you the son of God?' Except that you say and bring forward one of those who were with you and were condemned.

lemmas.gloss: of the things proposed by him

lemmas.form: οὐ τοῦ ἐν τῇ φύσει τῶν πραγμάτων

pass_b_english: We decided to address each of the points he raises, according to our ability, so that we would not appear to be dodging an answer because we are at a loss. We took care to follow not the natural connection and sequence of the matters themselves, but the order of the things written in his book. Come then, let us see what he says when he slanders the Holy Spirit, who was seen bodily by the Savior in the form of a dove. A Jew is still saying these things to him, and we confess that this Jew is our Lord Jesus. He says, 'When you were being baptized by John, you say that a phantom of a bird came down to you from the air.' Then the Jew who is with him, having inquired, says, 'Who is the worthy witness who saw the phantom, or who heard a voice from heaven calling you the Son of God? Nothing except that you yourself say it, and you bring forward one of those who were with you and were condemned.'

review.notes: Pass B contains a significant theological error/misreading of the Greek. The Greek 'πρὸς ὃν ὁμολογοῦμεν εἶναι κύριον ἡμῶν τὸν Ἰησοῦν' refers to the person to whom the Jew is speaking (Jesus), meaning 'to whom we confess Jesus to be our Lord'. Pass B translates this as 'and we confess that this Jew is our Lord Jesus', which incorrectly identifies the Jew as Jesus.
reasons: Pass B misidentifies the subject of confession: 'and we confess that this Jew is our Lord Jesus' contradicts the Greek 'πρὸς ὃν ὁμολογοῦμεν εἶναι κύριον ἡμῶν τὸν Ἰησοῦν' (to whom we confess Jesus to be our Lord).
Pass A omits the clause 'ἵνα δὲ μὴ δοκῶμεν ἑκόντες διὰ τὸ ἀπορεῖν ἀπαντήσεως ὑπερβαίνειν αὐτοῦ τὰ κεφάλαια' (source paragraph 1, line 1).

Pass B incorrectly states 'A Jew is still saying these things to him, and we confess that this Jew is our Lord Jesus' (source paragraph 1, line 5). This misrepresents the Greek, which says 'ὁ Ἰουδαῖος αὐτῷ ἔτι ταῦτα λέγων, πρὸς ὃν ὁμολογοῦμεν εἶναι κύριον ἡμῶν τὸν Ἰησοῦν'—the Jew is speaking to 'him' (Celsus), not to Jesus, and the speaker is not claiming the Jew is Jesus, but that the Jew is speaking to Jesus, whom we confess as Lord.

Pass B fails to cite the scripture reference for 'the Holy Spirit seen bodily by the Savior in the form of a dove' (source paragraph 1, line 5), which corresponds to Matthew 3:16 or Luke 3:22, but no citation is provided in the English translation.
